The curves $r=\sqrt{3}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ and $r=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ intersect for $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ at points $A$ and $B,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates $({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})$ and $({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})$ of the points $A$ and $B,$ respectively? Express the polar angles ${\theta }_{A}$ and ${\theta }_{B}$ in radians.

question.worked_solution:
To determine the polar coordinates of the intersection points, we will solve the following system of equations for $r$ and $\theta :$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}r=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ r=\sqrt{3}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

We begin by setting the equations equal to each other and solve for $\theta .$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\sqrt{3}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation in the interval $[0,2\pi ),$ we obtain ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{4\pi }{3}$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{3}.$

Now, we use the equation $r=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ to find the $r$-coordinates of the intersection points:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1} & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})=-4\,(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=2\sqrt{3} \\ {r}_{2} & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3})=-4\,(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates $({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})$ and $({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})$ of the points $A$ and $B,$ respectively, are

$$
({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})=(2\sqrt{3},\frac{4\pi }{3}),\,({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})=(2\sqrt{3},\frac{5\pi }{3}).
$$
